prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural-language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject, visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and, when interacting with objects, indicate whether the person is actively lifting, carrying, steadying, holding, arranging, or otherwise manipulating the object rather than using vague verbs. Specify direction of motion and movement relative to the frame or visible landmarks (toward/away from the viewer, toward/away from X, left/right side of the frame, up/down) and whether multiple motions are simultaneous. Describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, seated upright, leaning forward/back, crouching, squatting, kneeling, reclining, perched) and report gaze or attention only when head/eyes clearly indicate direction (e.g., eyes looking toward X). Give precise spatial relationships and approximate scale or distance (in front of, behind, next to, atop, a few feet/meters apart, to the left of) and state group density (isolated, a small group, a line, a crowd) when relevant. Describe observable lighting and shadow cues (directional backlight, side light, diffuse/overcast light, strong cast shadows and their direction/length) and note visible surface textures or effects such as wet pavement, puddles, reflections, ripples or choppy water, splashes, or motion blur. Keep the caption concrete and image-centered; avoid speculation, subjective judgments, or inferred intentions unless directly supported by clear visual evidence.
